title: Barnette’s conjecture
formal: Is every finite simple undirected graph that is 3-connected, cubic, bipartite and planar Hamiltonian?
definitions: A simple graph has neither loops nor parallel edges. It is 3-connected if it has at least four vertices and deleting any set of at most two vertices leaves a connected graph. Cubic means every vertex has degree exactly three. Bipartite means its vertices admit a partition into two sets with no edge having both endpoints in the same set. Planar means it has a drawing in the plane whose edge interiors do not intersect and contain no vertices; different edges may meet only at shared endpoints. A Hamiltonian cycle is a cyclic ordering \(v_{1},\ldots ,v_{n}\) of all vertices, each appearing exactly once, such that \(\{v_{i},v_{i+1}\}\) is an edge for every i, with \(v_{n+1}=v_{1}\). The cycle must use only edges already present in the graph. No algorithmic running-time guarantee is requested.
answer_criterion: Prove the proposition in the problem statement or its logical negation with the stated model, hypotheses and quantifier order. The proof must settle the entire target. A result conditional on an additional assumption settles only that conditional version. Benchmark acceptance requires a complete proof checked by a proof assistant and matching this statement.
why: Determine whether four basic structural conditions force a spanning cycle in every graph satisfying them.

importance.reason: A canonical and longstanding Hamiltonicity boundary with direct links between planar structure, graph traversal and drawing.

progress.text: Bekos, Kaufmann and Pfister improve a relaxed subhamiltonian-cycle guarantee to at least \(5n/6\) original edges; this is not a Hamiltonian cycle in the original graph.
Cambie and coauthors restate Barnette’s conjecture as open and study related planar partition problems.

context_blocks.text: Hamiltonicity is a global demand: one cycle must visit every vertex. Barnette’s conjecture proposes that planarity, bipartiteness, cubic degree and vertex connectivity together always guarantee this traversal.

The recent approximation result uses a subhamiltonian ordering whose consecutive pairs need not all be original edges. Its \(5n/6\) guarantee is substantial progress in a relaxed setting, but the missing adjacencies distinguish it from the requested cycle.

The planar dual connects the conjecture with partitions of Eulerian triangulations into induced forests. The 2026 partition paper makes those links precise while continuing to distinguish the unresolved Hamiltonicity assertion.

sentences: Barnette’s conjecture concerns 3-connected cubic bipartite planar graphs.
It predicts that every such graph contains a cycle through all vertices exactly once.
Every consecutive pair on the cycle must be an existing graph edge.
Relaxed book-embedding results may add missing adjacencies and therefore do not settle the conjecture.
The question isolates a classical boundary between local structural restrictions and a global spanning traversal.

status_note: Reviewed through 11 September 2026. The GD 2025 and February 2026 papers explicitly retain the conjecture; no general resolution was found.

notes: Defined 3-connectivity and required a Hamiltonian cycle in the original graph, not a planar supergraph.
